walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit 1: Speaking — a core area of A-Level Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit 1: Speaking brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit 1: Speaking.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which verb form correctly completes 'No creo que ___ justo'?
options: sea
es
será
siendo
However
Without luggage
Therefore
For example

mcqs.q: If you forget a Spanish word during the speaking exam, the best strategy is to do what?
options: Paraphrase the idea using Spanish you do know
Say the word in English
Stay silent until the examiner moves on
End the exam early

mcqs.q: 'Por un lado... por otro lado' is used to do what?
options: Contrast two sides of an argument
Give directions in the street
Describe physical appearance
Tell the time
All opinion phrases automatically trigger the subjunctive.
It must be followed by an infinitive with no subject.
No - affirmative 'creo que' takes the indicative; the subjunctive appears when the opinion is negated, as in 'no creo que sea'.
The subjunctive is only used in written Spanish, never in speech.

mcqs.q: Do long memorised monologues impress the examiner most?
options: The subjunctive is only used in written Spanish, never in speech.
No - the unit rewards spontaneous interaction: developing ideas, justifying opinions and responding naturally to follow-up questions.
Marks are awarded for speaking as fast as possible.

The subjunctive: 'Es importante que los jóvenes voten.'
It takes the indicative because it states a fact: 'es importante que votan'.
